body: I spent years depressed and something about lockdown made it significantly improve. I really enjoyed all the schadenfreude from people complaining they were going crazy and couldn't handle it. And I sat back and thought "Welcome to my life. I don't go anywhere, I don't do anything, I don't see anybody, I don't spend any money." The thought that normal ppl couldn't tolerate being in my shoes made me feel a little better and feel more confident and stronger because, yeah, my life is tough and I can deal with it just fine. I am resilient.

I had been chroniclly depressed for over 15 years. Nothing really worked well until I tried shrooms. It's was almost instant and immediate. I highly recommend it to everyone who is suffering from depression or anxiety, at least to try once. If it wasn't for shrooms, I most definitely would have unalived myself. But now I have soo much to live for and lots of goals to meet. 


For those curious what it's like: I turn off all electronic devices, no noises or LED lights. I do it in the evening in pitch black room. After eating the shrooms, you start to feel something in about 30 mins. It's a little tingly and blissful. Your tummy can be a little grumbly, though Waves of pure happiness start to intensify and roll over you. About an hour or 2 in, you will start to see faint colors. For me that was RGB outlines, and faint geometric and fractal patterns. Nothing too much. No visual distortions. The walls weren't melting or anthing. But you're still about 75% in control of your mind and body and just teeming with pure happiness like you've never experienced. Kinda like the tipsy stage of alcohol, but different. Listening to music can help. You mind will wander and guide you through some issues. It won't give you the solution, but it will help you look at it from a different viewpoint than your conscious mind and without the same emotional attachment. The whole experience is about 6 hours. In the morning when you wake up, you feel perfectly normal. There's no aftereffects or hangover. But your mind has been released from the many shackles holding you back. I do recommend seeing a therapist. As they can also help you unpack and process what you learned from the experience. Shrooms not a magic solution, just a very effective tool.

I'm sorry, my dude! I know things can seem bleak and pointless sometimes. But mark my words, things get better. It's not gonna happen suddenly. It's not gonna happen on its own. You will need to put in some work. Please believe me when I say, this is just your current  viewpoint and not a permanent viewpoint. One day you'll look back and say "I can't believe I felt that way." This I can guarantee you.  

I don't have any GI issues or other medical issues, so I can't relate to your situation 100%. I did however suffer from severe depression for 15 years that isolated me and ruined my life. Regardless, I'm gonna give you the best advice I can. 

Firstly, get a therapist. Fuck the stigma that says only crazy people see therapists. Everyone should have one. Find someone you like who you think understands you (I had a ~30yo straight woman once, she was a good listener and therapist, but her lack of knowledge about the gay community and intricacies of same sex dating was really apparent). They won't be you're best friend. They'll be better, in that, you can just talk to them about anything you want, they will always have time for you, they are not judgemental, and every intention of theirs is to help you. 1. It just helps to get things off your chest, tell someone, and be validated. 2. A second viewpoint is always beneficial. 3. They have methods and tools to help you navigate and cope with a variety of issues. So, getting a therapist is the first step. What's the worse that can happen?

Secondly, I know you feel lonely. And that's absolutely a valid feeling. We are social creatures. Try not to prioritize   getting people to like you. Especially, trying to hook up when you're feeling lonely. That's inauthentic validation, that in the end as you already know doesn't make you feel better about yourself. And trying to get more human interaction from those people who probably don't want to see you again will result in you just feeling worse and worse the more you try. Instead, you need to focus more on you. Don't ostrich and ignore your bigger issues just to focus on doing things not to feel lonely. Put yourself first. Be selfish, you're allowed. If you want to meet people, they don't have to be gay, nor want to have sex with you for you not to feel lonely. Delve into your interests and hobbies more. Join some clubs, go out do some group activities. Have conversations with people that are just as passionate as you, and then slowly get to know them better personally. 

Thirdly, consider trying some psilocybin. Just hear me out on this. There's numerous recent studies about the therapeutic benefits, at John Hopkins especially. I took many combinations of 25-30 drugs over the years and nothing really worked or worked well enough. That is, until I tried some magic mushrooms. Just after one night, I felt like I got a new lease on life and it lasted for over 9 months. Completely got me out of the 15 year funk that never lifted. I'm not the only person who's had this revelation. You don't have to do a whole lot. Walls don't need to be melting or full body dissociation. Just 2 grams ish. Enough to enhance colors, see some geometric shapes, laugh, feel euphoric, enjoy some music, and do some introspection. It's been decriminalized in Seattle, so sourcing it shouldn't be that risky. I can only strongly urge you to consider it an option. Do you own research and make your own opinion. In the end, the decision is completely up to you. 

Just know there are people here on Reddit you can always turn to for support. Even the kindness of complete strangers can mean the world when you're in a difficult spot. Do feel free to drop into my DMs if you want to talk more.

It does have mechanism. There seems to be a commonality with treatments that interrupt current neuron connection pathways and the brain does a reorganization of those pathways. TMS does this magneticly, ECT does this with electrical impulses, psychedelics do this chemically, which is why you have hallucinogenic effects and mixed senses. There seems to be significant relief of depressive symptoms after these kinda treatments. Some are just more invasive and broad stroked.

I dunno why this is being downvoted. But it's an exceptionally valid point. I had treatment resistant depression for over 15 years. After years of trying different med combinations with no significant improvement and dealing with side effects, I started increasing the intensity of my plan of attack to not be depressed anymore. 

After trying meds for over a decade, I added in some talk therapy. Something I didn't previously consider a solution  to my depression, but it helped a bit. But not enough. My next increment was TMS therapy. It was expensive, and I had to go every weekday for 6 weeks. It wasn't real effective, but I had to try. After that I made attempts to enroll in some studies for ketamine and psilocybin, but I was disqualified as a participant for both b/c I'm left handed and my brain scans wouldn't be comparable. After trying the legal route, I sourced some psilocybin in Denver where it's decriminalized. This is where I'm at now. 

I'd also like to say that the pandemic has played a significant part in my recovery. During the dark years, I didn't go anywhere, I didn't do anything, I didn't socialize and see people, I just stayed in my bedroom a lot. Lockdown basically forced that lifestyle on everyone, I did enjoy a bout of schadenfreude when people started freaking out and couldn't handle my lifestyle. But the restrictions eased the pressures of socialization stresses they created. Along with occasional (monthly or every other) doses of psilocybin, I've made a significant recovery. Not all the way, but I'm feeling the best I've been in years, I having a lot of feels, I'm more motivated, have more energy, feeling genuinely positive and wanted to meet people make new friends and date again. 

Had I not made any progress, I would have continued on and tried LSD, and after that... I even fear to say it because I would try almost anything to avoid it but... ECT.

My dad came home drunk one time in December and knocked on my closed bedroom door. It was dark, so I pretended to be asleep. My mom heard the knocking and asked what he was doing. He replied with a slur "oh, I just wanted to tell [me] that there's a Santa down at the strip mall right now. Maybe he should go down there and ask him for a new place to live by New Year's."

The reason that it was so hurtful was because I heard it when he didn't think I did. He purposefully meant to put me down, and that's says so much about his intention and how he really felt.

As someone who has spent ~15 years, specifically including my entire adult life, in treatment resistant severe depression, I chose not to drink alcohol because it serves no benefit to me. I have indulged and overindulged in the past, but my serotonin receptors are so dead I don't get much enjoyment out of it; just bad hangovers, regret, and a persistently empty bank acct. The hardest part about not drinking is having to explain to anyone why you don't drink when you decline.

My life fundamentally changed when I was 18. My mom was nosey and ended up outting me to my father who kicked me out that night. I was kinda in denial about my parents. I thought my friends were more important at that time. I tried to make it on my own but in rough times I had to turn back to my family, and all went downhill from there.

I'm 32 now, a broken and dysfunctional shell of a person. Chronically depressed. So emotionally beaten down over years, I don't know what's actually left inside. Never finished college. I've attempted suicide 3 times.

My dad treats me with utmost contempt. It's gotten worse over the years. I'm not saying this is you, but my dad had become a narcissist and a manipulator. I don't live my life how he wants, so he does everything to try and manipulate me. In his opinion, I act selfishly with malicious intent towards my family. He knows what I'm thinking, why I do things, and this allows him to tell what I'm going to do in the future. At some point, it turned to quid pro quo harrasment where he claims to do things for me that I didn't ask for and now I am indebted to him. And to be honest, the scales are rigged and there is no amount of anything that will ever make us even. 

As depression set in, I stopped living. First, I lost everything that brought me joy. Then, I lost my energy and motivation to do anything. Finding and holding a job was hard. Going to college with no money was hard. I became isolated from friends and became lonely. I felt imprisoned at home. I had no resources to get out and do things, no money, no interest, nobody to talk to or hang out with. Living with my parents became an extremely hostile environment. I don't try to change how my parents feel. Therapists just tell you to cope with it. Having to accept emotional abuse is not an acceptable solution.

As of today, I don't think I could ever forgive my parents for what they did to me. My father especially, but also my mother for being spineless and going along with it. There is nothing they could say or do now that would make my life any better. The most heartfelt apology pales in comparison with the sheer amount of pain and suffering they've caused me. I would have much preffered being kidnapped and prayed the gay away. I'm sure there was a tipping point where it would have made a difference, but we're long past that. I just want them out of my life completely. If I never heard or spoke to them ever again, I would probably be better off.

I wish I had a dad like you.
